sentences.text: This ancient marine reptile is defined by a unique nose structure featuring an external opening split by a pillar.
It also possesses a long front section of the upper jaw that extends up to the level of the nasal bone.
The type specimen, cataloged as YKM 65119, was found in Early Cretaceous deposits within Ulyanovsk Oblast, Russia.
Another identification lists the holotype as SGU 104a/22, comprising a fragmentary skull and vertebral column from the Hauterivian stage.
The genus was formally described by Ochev and Efimov in 1985.
Simbirskiasaurus is classified as an extinct genus of ichthyosaur belonging to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
It is placed within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
This animal lived during the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago, specifically between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
